consumer_contexts: rhythm-action and object-interaction XR games distributed on a headset store (Meta Horizon Store, PICO store) that must pass an entitlement check at launch and report achievements and leaderboard scores per signed-in account without hand-writing a vendor SDK call at every gameplay site

spatial-creation and training XR applications distributed through Steam or a visionOS App Store build that save small per-account cloud documents and read them back on a second device, behind the same typed intent seam regardless of which store's SDK is wired in
common_kernel: account and provider identity as validated identities separate from any vendor SDK session, token, or account object

a closed platform-service capability set (entitlement, achievement, leaderboard, cloud_save, identity), with a provider descriptor built by explicit registration declaring which capabilities a given provider supports so a composition fails closed at compose time when a required capability is missing

typed check_entitlement, unlock, report_score, read_leaderboard, cloud_write, and cloud_read intents applied to an immutable state with stable failure codes and deterministic replay to an equal fingerprint

an entitlement check as a distinct, boot-time, asynchronous request/response call that can fail for reasons other than being not entitled, and that a store's own certification requirements expect a title to perform and to fail closed on
achievement unlock and leaderboard score submission as idempotent, per-account write calls addressed to a server-defined identifier, with leaderboard reads as a separate paginated query
cloud save as a small per-account document or key/value store distinct from achievements and leaderboards, with an explicit conflict or staleness signal rather than a silent overwrite
an offline pending-write queue keyed by an idempotency key so a write issued without connectivity replays in order exactly once when connectivity returns, rather than being lost or duplicated
configurable_variation: which providers a product registers, which capabilities each provider supports, and the cloud payload guard rail per provider
which achievements, leaderboards, and cloud keys a product defines and their content

adapter-side provider selection (Meta Horizon Platform SDK, PICO platform SDK, Steamworks, Apple Game Center and StoreKit, Unity Gaming Services Cloud Save) and the consumer-owned fallback intent behind the entitlement gate
consumer-owned store listing, purchase flow, and account-management UI
excluded_project_specific: one product's store listing, purchase flow, pricing, and account-management screen content
one project's choice of which achievements, leaderboards, or cloud keys to expose and any judgement that a store's review outcome is acceptable
rationale: Platform services (entitlement, achievements, leaderboards, cloud save, and identity behind a signed-in account) is a recurring cross-project need the shipped-game-gap-matrix records for every benchmark shape, and its kernel (validated account and provider identity, a closed capability set with an explicit provider descriptor that fails composition closed when a capability is missing, typed intents over an immutable state with deterministic replay, and an idempotency-keyed offline pending-write queue) is supported by Meta's and PICO's first-party platform SDK documentation for entitlement, achievements, leaderboards, and cloud storage, Valve's Steamworks documentation for achievements, stats, leaderboards, and cloud files, Apple's Game Center and StoreKit documentation including visionOS-applicable entitlement verification, Unity Gaming Services' engine-side Cloud Save as a document-shaped alternative, Apple's App Store Review Guidelines as store-policy evidence that a working entitlement or restore check is a certification requirement, and two independent open-source implementations (the long-maintained Steamworks.NET wrapper and the second-engine GodotSteam integration) that expose the same four-capability shape as plain typed calls with asynchronous, checkable results, while every product keeps its own store listing, purchase flow, and account-management UI outside the shared Core.
non_claims: Admission does not claim that any store granted entitlement, unlocked an achievement, accepted a leaderboard score, or persisted a cloud file, nor any named-provider, named-store, or named-account behavior; the family guarantees the plumbing only and every such judgement is a human or process observation in a store sandbox log or a Device Lab receipt.

Admission does not make the family a storefront, a purchasing flow, or an account-management screen, and it transfers no Persistence, Settings, Interaction, Audio, or Haptics evidence to this family; evidence for one provider, store, or account tuple never transfers to another.
